status_reason: The full paper was read and both experiments are rebuilt with its parameters, but a modern display's red and green primaries replace the paper's CRT phosphors, so the 40% colour grating and the yellow mean are matched in luminance (the paper's 45 cd/m2 and red:green split), not in chromaticity or cone contrast; the colour stimuli need rig-specific photometry, and 49 unstated details are ASSUMED.

original.citation: Cavanagh, P. (1992). Attention-based motion perception. Science, 257(5076), 1563–1565.
original.experiments: Experiment 1 (attentive tracking of colour vs luminance bars, with the motion null and thresholds of Fig. 1) and Experiment 2 (apparent speed of a colour grating, global vs tracking match, Fig. 2)

assets.source: drawn by src/cavanagh1992/preview.py from the parameter files

notes: Colour stimuli need a linearised display (alhazen calibrate gamma) and each gun's maximum luminance measured with a photometer in configs/photometry-<rig>.yaml. Run equiluminance-speed for each subject first; later tasks refuse a real session without it. A scroll wheel works as the knob but the arrow keys suffice.
